<thought>Using the retrieved retrosynthetic template, the reaction breaks the amide C–N bond, giving an amine (aniline) and the corresponding carboxylic acid. The two precursors that recombine via this template to form the target molecule are:
1. The carboxylic‑acid fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1  
2. Aniline: c1ccccc1N

Thus the list of possible precursor combinations is a single list containing these two SMILES.</thought>
<final_answer>[[\"Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1\", \"c1ccccc1N\"]]</final_answer>
